primary_sources.source: Alan K. Mackworth, Consistency in Networks of Relations, Artificial Intelligence 8(1) 99-118, 1977
primary_sources.scope: Arc consistency and local removal of unsupported values are historical motivations; the selected law is the finite binary relation support projection, NOT all of AC-3 graph scheduling

candidate.input_contract: (Dx, Dy, R) each finite canonical sorted unique lists of exact integers; R is finite lexicographically sorted unique list of [x,y] exact-int pairs. Dx,Dy may be empty and R may be empty. Input violation produces ERROR, never silently reorders or coerces.
candidate.result_contract: Let M={ (x,y) in R : x in Dx and y in Dy }. When M is empty return NO-SUPPORT (not a set of newly invented values). Otherwise return SUPPORTED(sorted unique projection_x(M), sorted unique projection_y(M)). No pair outside R is certified, and supported value in each output has an existential compatible value in the other output. Returns no witness to a globally satisfiable larger constraint network.
falsifiers: A value x with no R-related y in the current Dy must be removed; keeping x violates sound support pruning.
Arbitrary Cartesian product of output domains is NOT guaranteed to be contained in R; do not claim universal pair compatibility or global CSP solution.
When all allowed pairs are removed, return named NO-SUPPORT rather than SUCCESS(empty,empty), avoiding contradictory proof status.
Monotonicity: reducing either input domain cannot invent any supported output; repeated projection must be idempotent.
Reject unsorted/duplicate finite lists, float/boolean values, non-pair relation members: no silent coercion into semantic identity.
invariants: extensive-contraction: supported domains subset corresponding input domains
local-arc-support: every retained value has at least one partner in original relation
idempotence of support projection on same relation
symmetry under swapping variables and transposing relation
monotonicity with respect to restricting input domains
when R has no compatible tuples, NO-SUPPORT
candidate.type_warning: Pure finite pairwise support projection. Not D2 branching/syntax, a CLP solver, arc-consistency closure of arbitrary graphs, database join identity, Forth native stack action, CUDA/FPGA instruction or trained/neural AI.
